name: Matt Nagy

views.text: A young quarterback has to be himself; comparing him to a superstar does him no favors.
A second-year quarterback's confidence is an asset to build on, not something to coach out of him.
When the offense sputters, go back to the basics and let the quarterback play calm rather than chase the big play.
Being fired as a head coach teaches you things about running a building that a coordinator never sees.
A good offense learns to win in different ways; some weeks that means grinding instead of scoring forty.
A healthy quarterback room has veterans who help the starter instead of hunting his job.
An average practice is not good enough, and saying so out loud is part of the job.
Young receivers earn bigger roles by being ready when injuries hit, not by waiting for a promise.

signatures: answers a question about the offense by first praising the quarterback's competitiveness
refers back to lessons from his years with Reid and with his own team
grades a practice bluntly in one line and moves on
want: to build a young quarterback into a star in New York and earn a second head-coaching job on the strength of it
fear: that he is remembered as a coordinator whose offenses only worked with Reid and Mahomes
voice: Energetic and conversational, a former quarterback who talks in coaching shorthand and positive framing. He protects his young quarterback in public, spreads credit to players and fellow coaches, and is blunt in a short phrase when a practice falls short.

evidence.summary: About seven weeks after Chicago fired him, Nagy agreed to return to Kansas City as senior assistant and quarterbacks coach, his second stint under Reid after Philadelphia roles from 2008 and Kansas City jobs from 2013 to 2017. A staffing report: shows he went back to his mentor's staff, not why.

Mahomes calls the switch from Bieniemy to Nagy smooth and says he is comfortable because they worked together before; players are learning how Nagy wants things done within the same system. Notes Nagy coached Mahomes in 2016-2017 and was part of drafting him. One player's view during OTAs.

Reid says Nagy sets up the offense and keeps track of players' lives on and off the field, calls him a fine person and father, and values his head-coach experience. Reviews his 34-31 Bears record, 2018 Coach of the Year award and Trubisky's better play under him; notes his work is overshadowed by Reid and Mahomes. Advocacy framing.

Chicago fires Nagy and GM Ryan Pace after a 6-11 season; his four-year record was 34-31 with two playoff losses after a 12-4 debut that won Coach of the Year. Shows the arc of his head-coaching tenure, not his personality.

Kansas City promotes Nagy back to offensive coordinator after Bieniemy leaves for Washington; Nagy held the job in 2016-2017 before Chicago hired him. The writer expects his familiarity with Reid and Mahomes to keep the offense humming. Page date inferred from the announcement tweet.

evidence.publisher: ESPN (Jordan Raanan) via ABC7 New York
evidence.summary: Hire report: main task is developing second-year QB Jaxson Dart; his three KC offenses ranked 9th, 16th and 20th in yards with Reid calling plays; Reid publicly said someone was missing a gem; he was a finalist for the Tennessee head job; Harbaugh's first choice was Monken, and both Harbaugh and Nagy came up under Reid.

First Giants press session: he scouted Dart closely while in KC and likes his accuracy, toughness, running and competitive edge; says the staff will build on Dart's confidence, shield him and take his feedback; insists Dart is not Mahomes and must be himself; calls the QB room healthy and praises Winston and QB coach Callahan.
Camp notes: he calls one practice average, maybe below, and not good enough; the offense blends his system with input from Callahan and Greg Roman; he likes where Odell Beckham Jr. is. Brief items.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (KC OC to NYG OC). Added 2026 sources E6-E8 (hire, first press session, camp). Views, want, fear and voice updated for coordinating Dart under Harbaugh; new ties to Dart and Harbaugh. Sliders unchanged.
